newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL RUBBER UP AT NOON ON TECHNICAL ADJUSTMENT.
newsitem.headline: KL RUBBER UP AT NOON ON TECHNICAL ADJUSTMENT.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were higher at noon as the market adjusted again to the weakness of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar, traders said.
"It's still early in the day and we're hoping to get some inquiries, but otherwise, things are quiet," said a trader.
At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the RSS1 for September buyer at 249 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up one cent from Tuesday's close.
The SMR20 for September buyer was half cent higher at 248 cents a kg.
Trading houses were offering the SMR 20 at 248 cents a kg, SMR CV at 289, SMR L at 270, SMR 5 at 260, SMR 10 at 250 and drum latex at 192, all for Aug/Sep.
Traders said prices could rise again in the afternoon if the ringgit remained under pressure. The ringgit has fallen nearly 12 percent in value against the dollar in the last month.
"The currency is the only factor at the moment," said a trader. "There is no real buying."
At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7730 to a dollar in Kuala Lumpur, recovering from the opening an 2.7785.
